2027-02-17.title: Wednesday of the second week of the Great Fast
readings: Christ, in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom
The Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head
2027-02-17.verse: But Jesus said to him, “Follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead.”
theo: Twice in five verses Genesis repeats the same words: “that very day.” Abraham “circumcised the flesh of their foreskins that very day, as God had said to him… That very day Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised.” He was ninety-nine years old. He did not form a committee or wait for a more convenient season. God spoke, and Abraham obeyed the same day, beginning with himself and then with all his household. Delay is one of the quiet enemies of the Fast. We mean to pray more, to make our confession, to be reconciled, to give alms; and the days slip by. The Psalmist prays the opposite: “I hurry and do not delay to keep your commandments.”

In the Gospel two men approach Jesus. The first is eager: “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.” Jesus tells him the cost: “Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.” The second wants to follow, but later: “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.” Jesus answers: “Follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead.” St John Chrysostom explains that the Lord was not teaching contempt for parents; he was teaching that nothing, not even the most honourable duty, may be placed before following him (in substance). Why is he worth it? Paul gives the answer: in Christ “are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.” Paul struggles in prayer so that the hearts of the Colossians may be “encouraged and united in love,” and he rejoices to see “the firmness of your faith in Christ.” The one who has no place to lay his head is himself the treasure.
outline: Ask: what have you been meaning to do for God, but keep postponing?
live: Take one good resolution of this Fast that you have postponed and do it before the day ends.
Spend fifteen minutes today reading the Gospel slowly, as someone searching for treasure.
2027-02-17.prayer: Lord Jesus, you had nowhere to lay your head, yet in you are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. Give us the promptness of Abraham, who obeyed that very day. Free us from excuses and delays, unite our hearts in love, and make our faith firm, so that we may follow you wherever you go. Amen.
altar: The Son of Man who had nowhere to lay his head makes his dwelling among us on the altar, and in us when we receive him.

quick: In Christ are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
Jesus asks us to follow him without delay or excuse.
2027-02-17.action: Do today one good thing you have been postponing.
2027-02-17.question: What do I put first before following Jesus?

family.explain: Some people wanted to follow Jesus, but said: later, not now. Jesus said: follow me now. Abraham also obeyed God the same day he heard him. When God asks something good of us, the best time is today.
family.intention: We pray that our family may not delay in doing good.
family.ask: Ask: “What good thing have we been saying we will do later?”

illus: A young mother in Kattappana kept a list on the fridge of people she meant to visit: an aunt in hospital, a friend who had lost her husband, a neighbour who had moved away. Every week the list grew. One Lent she decided to cross off one name each week, whatever happened. In the third week she visited the aunt in hospital, who held her hand for an hour and told her stories of her own mother. The aunt died the following Tuesday. The young woman still keeps the list, but now it is short.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, we want to follow you. Take away our delays and our excuses. Amen.
share: That very day Abraham obeyed (Genesis 17:26). What have I been postponing that God asked of me?
All the treasures of wisdom and knowledge (Colossians 2:3). Do I treat Christ as my greatest treasure?
Lord, first let me go (Matthew 8:21). What do I put first?
interc: For those who are discerning a call to priesthood or religious life.
For the homeless and all who have nowhere to lay their heads.
For those who keep postponing their return to God.
For families grieving the death of a parent.
For unity and love among the members of our parish.
pm.close: Father, your Son had nowhere to lay his head, yet he is our treasure. Give us hearts that obey without delay and follow him wherever he goes. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Genesis says it twice: that very day. Abraham, ninety-nine years old, obeyed God's command that very day, beginning with himself and his household (Genesis 17:23, 26).
Delay is a quiet enemy of the Fast. We mean to pray, to confess, to forgive, to give; and the days slip by. The Psalmist says: I hurry and do not delay to keep your commandments (Psalm 119:60).

In the Gospel one man promises: I will follow you wherever you go. Another says: first let me go and bury my father. Jesus answers: the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head... Follow me (Matthew 8:19–22). Nothing may come before him, not even good things.
Why is he worth it? Because in him are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge (Colossians 2:3). Let us not wait for a better season. Today is the day to follow. Amen.
kids: Children, when God asked Abraham to do something, he did it that very day! When Jesus says follow me, let us not say later, later. Is there something good your mum or dad asked you to do? Do it today, with a smile.

intro: Abraham's prompt obedience, the treasure hidden in Christ, and the call that will not wait.

concl: God's word is best obeyed on the day it is heard.
The one who had nowhere to lay his head is the treasure worth everything.
2027-02-17.resolve: Each day of this week, do at once the first good thing God puts in your heart.
